sentences.text: No. - 286 of 2023 Appellant :- The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Thru.
Its Legal Cell 94 Hazratganj Lko.

Respondent :- Ram Sahay And 6 Others Counsel for Appellant :- Ashok Kumar Rai,Ashish Jaiswal Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
1. Heard Shri Ashish Jaiswal, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. The instant appeal has been preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 against the award dated 14.06.2023 passed in M.A.C.P. No.211/2017 whereby in a death case the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.6,50,800/- along with 7.5% interest per annum in favour of the claimants/respondents.

3. The sole question which has been raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the Tribunal has erred in granting a higher compensation inasmuch as the age of the deceased was taken as 55 years on the basis of the postmortem report.
His submission is that the son of the deceased, who was examined as a witness stated that his age was 46 years.

It is thus sought to be The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... vs Ram Sahay And 6 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51114506/
1 argued that in case if the son was 46 years that apparently the age of the deceased could not have been 55 years, rather it should have been over 60 and this aspect has not been appropriately considered by the Tribunal.
4.

sentences.text: Having considered the aforesaid submission and before adverting to the merits thereof it will be worth while to take a glance at the facts giving rise the instant appeal.

5. The claimants had filed a claim petition bearing No.211 of 2017 before M.A.C.P., Lakhimpur Kheri with the averment that on 07.09.2016 the deceased, namely, Komal Prasad was travelling in Tempo bearing No. U.P. 31 T 2689.

Since the driver of the Tempo was rash and negligent accordingly the Tempo overturned, as a result, the father of the claimants, namely, Komal Prasad received grievous injury and though he was taken to the hospital but he was declared brought dead.
It is in the aforesaid context the claim petition was filed wherein it was also stated that the deceased was 55 years of age and was a vegetable vendor in the village.
6. The claim petition came to be contested by the owner as well as the Insurance Company and it was stated that the vehicle in question was duly insured along with the necessary documents.

The driver of the Tempo also possessed a valid and subsisting driving license and for the aforesaid reason, if at all any compensation is awarded the same was liable to be identified by the Insurance Company.

7. The Insurance Company on the other hand had raised the general defences that unless it is proved that the vehicle was being driven in accordance with the policy conditions other than that the liability may not be fastened on the Insurance Company.
8.
The Tribunal had framed five issues.

In so far as the finding returned regarding the rash and negligence driving of the Tempo driver, the involvement of the Tempo in the accident and the death of Komal Prasad from the accident is concerned, the same is not under challenge before this Court.

The Tribunal after holding that the driver of the Tempo in question was rash and negligent and the tempo was duly insured and had a valid license went on to compute the compensation and taking a notional income of the deceased has awarded a sum of Rs.6,50,800/- along with 7.5% interest by means of award dated 14.06.2023 which is the subject matter of the instant appeal.
9. In the aforesaid backdrop, if the records are seen by the Court, it would be found that there is a clear statement that the deceased was 55 years of age and was a vegetable vendor in village.
10. From the perusal of the statement given by one of the claimants, who was the son of the deceased.
He has stated that his age was about 50 years.

In his cross-examination, though a minor suggestion was placed to suggest that the age of the deceased was more than 65 years, accordingly, it is sought to be taken as a benefit to create a ground that the age of the deceased could not have been 55 years.
11. Be that as it may, this Court finds that insofar as the Insurance Company is concerned on the aforesaid issue there was no challenge nor any evidence was led.

It is also to be seen that the The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... vs Ram Sahay And 6 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51114506/
2 claimants as well as the deceased they all have a rural background.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There was nothing on record to prove that the age of the deceased was not 55 years.

Neither any positive evidence was led before the Tribunal by the Insurance Company except to give a suggestion to contradict that the age of the deceased was not 55 years rather was more than 65 years.

Merely because a suggestion has been put in the cross-examination of one of the witness which was turned down is not going to give any leverage to the appellants, who said that the age of the deceased has been incorrectly taken as 55 years.
12. On the other hand, the Tribunal apart from the statement of claimants that the deceased was 55 years which was also recorded in the postmortem report.

Though it is clear that the postmortem may not be an accurate assessment for the age but nevertheless in absence of any other evidence but it is some sort of evidence which has a semblance and authenticity which can be taken to be basis for calculating the age.

It is in this view of the matter, the Tribunal has taken the age of the deceased as 55 years and thereafter noticing the same it has made the calculation which is in accordance with law and the Court does not find that there is any patent illegality in the award which may persuade this Court to interfere in the award dated 14.06.2023.
13. For the aforesaid reasons, the Court is of the clear opinion that the appeal sans merit and accordingly, is dismissed at the admission stage.
In the facts and circumstances, there shall be no order as to cost.
14. Any amount deposited by the appellants before this Court, shall be remitted to the Tribunal to be released in favour of the claimant-respondents.

The remaining amount if any shall also be paid by the appellant to the claimants-respondents in accordance with the award within a period of 60 days from the date a copy of this Order is placed before the Tribunal.
